title: How do you focus stacking to photograph a bracelet?
metaTitle: 🔍 Focus stacking bracelet: clear and accurate photo
description: 📷 Capture every detail of your bracelets with Orbitvu. A 9-step guide to sharp, professional macro visuals.
tool: Orbitvu station software and a bracelet
introText:
🔍 The Focus Stacking, or focus stacking, is a reference technique in macro photography and jewelry packshot.

It is essential in the workflows of Professional jewelry shooting, in particular to accurately reproduce the textures, reliefs and volumes of complex parts such as bracelets, rings or cufflinks.

By automatically combining several sharpness planes, this method makes it possible to generate a completely clear product image, from the foreground to the background — a key requirement in commercial watch photography or for e-commerce content with high added value.

steps.title: Positioning and choice of the template
steps.content:
Before shooting, clean your band thoroughly to avoid any visible imperfection in macro.

📍 Position it in the exact center of the automated photo studio, using a invisible fixing kit (transparent double-sided adhesive) to ensure a stable and professional look. Then select in Orbitvu Station the shooting template adapted to the type of your jewelry (rigid, precious, textured bracelet...), or create a custom template for your collection. This step is essential to ensure the reproducibility visuals and maintain a product visual consistency, especially in luxury jewelry.
steps.structuredText: Start by cleaning your bracelet to avoid any imperfection. Position it correctly on the center point of the photo studio, using an invisible support kit (transparent double-sided adhesive) for an optimal result. Once your bracelet is in place, choose the default shooting template in the software corresponding to the type of jewelry you are capturing (simple, precious or complex bracelet) or create your own template.

steps.title: Light and camera settings
steps.content:
⚙️ Adjust light and camera settings in the station software Orbitvu in order to capture your bracelet in an optimal way. To avoid unwanted reflections, be sure to limit the ambient light.

Here are the settings we can recommend:

🔍 Use a macro lens to capture fine details.

📷 Opt for a wide aperture (f/2.8 to f/4) in order to obtain a shallow depth of field.

✔ Set the value ISO between 100 and 200 max to reduce image noise.

⚖️ Set the white balance depending on the lighting in your environment.

💡 Finally, adjust the The lighting of the studio to your liking and adapt it to the surface of the bracelet (matt or glossy).

For more precision, check out our guide to camera settings for jewelry photography.

steps.title: Using Superfocus (Wizard)
steps.content:
Click on the assistant Superfocus (wizard) from the software interface Orbitvu Station.💻

This assistant will guide automatically the different stages of stacking by suggesting the ideal parameters for focus stacking.
steps.structuredText: Click on the Superfocus Wizard from the Orbitvu Station software interface. This assistant will automatically guide the various stacking steps by suggesting the ideal settings for focus stacking.

steps.title: 1st stacking stage - focus on the front area
steps.content:
🎬Start the sequence by placing the first focus on the Front area of the bracelet, that is to say the foreground.

This makes it possible to capture all precise details of the areas closest to the objective.
steps.structuredText: Start the sequence by placing the first focus on the front area of the wristband, i.e. the foreground. This makes it possible to capture all the precise details of the areas closest to the lens.

steps.title: 2nd stacking stage - focus on the back area
steps.content:
Move the focus gradually to rear part of the bracelet.

🔍 Zoom can be used here to ensure that fine details, like carvings or stones, are captured accurately.
steps.structuredText: Move the focus gradually to the back of the bracelet. Zoom can be used here to ensure that fine details, like carvings or stones, are captured accurately.

steps.title: 3rd stage of stacking - the size of the steps between the focuses
steps.content:
Set the size of the steps (or increments) between shots.

One smallness Of step is Recommended for bracelets that are complex or have fine details. This ensures that all areas of the object are perfectly clear.
steps.structuredText: Set the size of the steps (or increments) between shots. A small step size is recommended for bracelets that are complex or have fine details. This ensures that all areas of the object are in perfect sharpness.

steps.title: 4th stage of stacking - number of steps for focusing
steps.content:
Determine the number of steps to complete for full focus stacking. The number of steps required for focus stacking Depends on the opening of your objective and the complexity of the object.

The larger the aperture, the shallower the depth of field, and the more you'll need intermediate photos.
steps.structuredText: Determine the number of steps to complete for full focus stacking. The number of steps required for focus stacking depends on the aperture of your lens and the complexity of the object. The larger the aperture, the shallower the depth of field, and the more intermediate shots you'll need.

steps.title: Image editing and retouching
steps.content:
Once the images are compiled, you can move on to editing. 🎨

The software offers several options, such asadjustment of colors, brightness, contrast, fine details, as well as numerous other improvements to refine the image and achieve the desired result.

Ensure that the final result Remain faithful to your jewelry.

Make sure that the final result stays true to your jewelry.

steps.title: Exporting images
steps.content:
Once the editing is complete, select the export format (s) according to the intended use, such as JPEG, TIFF, or PNG if you want to keep a high image quality and the possibility of transparency.

You can also create a Template for these parameters in order to save time for future exports. 📂

Finalize the export, and your bracelet design is ready to be used! 📤

faqs.question: Is it more cost effective to use an automated studio for jewelry photography?
faqs.answer: Yes, an automated studio optimizes the entire workflow, from shooting to exporting. It allows serial shooting and the reuse of saved settings, reducing production time and the costs associated with errors or retakes.

faqs.question: Is there a need for training if the software is intuitive?
faqs.answer: Even though the software is designed to be simple, training allows you to discover advanced tips, such as customizing templates, managing complex lighting, or optimizations specific to jewelry photography.

faqs.question: Does focus stacking with Orbitvu Station take a long time to complete?
faqs.answer: No, thanks to the built-in Superfocus Assistant, focus stacking with Orbitvu Station is fast and automated. The software guides every step, from initial focus to image fusion, reducing the time required compared to manual setup. The duration depends primarily on the complexity of the product and the number of images required, but for a standard bracelet, this only takes a few minutes.

faqs.question: Do I have to fix my bracelet before doing a focus stacking?
faqs.answer: Yes, securing the band is essential to avoid movement between shots and to ensure perfect sharpness. Use an invisible fixing kit for a professional look.

faqs.question: Can we create a 360° animation with focus stacking?
faqs.answer: Yes, focus stacking can be combined with 360° animation to get sharp views from any angle. The software automatically adjusts the focus to each angle before generating the animation.
